2026-12-17.title: 17 December · Advent Weekday (O Wisdom)
readings: The scepter shall not depart from Judah
Justice shall flourish in his time, and fullness of peace for ever
The genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham
2026-12-17.alt: From today the readings follow the date. The “O Antiphons” begin at Vespers and as Gospel Acclamations: today, O Sapientia (O Wisdom).
2026-12-17.verse: An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
theo: Today the final stretch of Advent begins. The readings now follow the calendar date, and the Church sings the great “O Antiphons”. Today's: “O Wisdom, who came from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end and ordering all things mightily and sweetly: come and teach us the way of prudence” (cf. Wisdom 8:1). Jacob blesses Judah: “The scepter shall not depart from Judah… until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his.”

Matthew opens with a genealogy: forty-two generations in three groups of fourteen, from Abraham to David to the exile to Christ. It contains saints and sinners, kings and nobodies, and, unusually, four women (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah), some foreigners, some with complicated stories. God's plan runs through real, messy family history. Then the pattern breaks: “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born.” Jesus enters our family tree as a true man and true Son of God.
outline: Ask: do you know your family tree? Who in it would you rather not mention?
Christ, the Wisdom of God, orders all things.
God keeps his promises across centuries.
“Of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah.”
live: Pray today for your ancestors, living and dead, by name.
Pray today's O Antiphon each morning and evening.
2026-12-17.prayer: O Wisdom, who came forth from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end and ordering all things mightily and sweetly: come and teach us the way of prudence. Bless my family and all its history. Amen.
altar: At Mass we join the long line of generations who waited for Christ and now receive him.

quick: The O Antiphons begin: O Wisdom, come!
God kept his promise to Judah across centuries.
Jesus enters a real, messy family history.
2026-12-17.action: Pray for your ancestors by name.
2026-12-17.question: Do I believe God can work through my family's story?

family.explain: Jesus had a family tree, with grandparents and great-grandparents, some good and some who made mistakes. God loved them all.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and ancestors, living and dead.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family taught us about Jesus?”

pm.open: O Wisdom, coming from the mouth of the Most High, come and teach us the way of prudence. Lord Jesus, as we gather in this last week of Advent, guide us by your wisdom. Amen.
share: Jesus' family tree includes saints and sinners (Matthew 1:1–17). What does that tell me about God's love for my family?
Who handed on the faith to me, and have I thanked God for them?
What decision do I need God's wisdom for now?
pm.resp: O Wisdom, come and teach us.
interc: For the Church, that she may be guided by the Wisdom of God.
For our ancestors who handed on the faith, that they may rest in peace.
For families wounded by sin and division, that Christ may heal them from within.
For those making important decisions, that they may receive wisdom.
For our group, that we may prepare well for Christmas.
pm.close: Lord God, you entered our human family through a long line of generations. Bless our families, heal our history, and teach us the wisdom of your Son. Amen.

illus: A family in Kuravilangad keeps a book with the names of their ancestors back seven generations, some saints, some sinners. Every Christmas they pray for all of them. The grandmother says: “Jesus has a family tree with crooked branches too.”

homily: Dear friends, from today the Church enters the last week before Christmas. At Evening Prayer she begins to sing the great O Antiphons. Tonight's is: O Wisdom, coming forth from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end and ordering all things mightily and sweetly: come and teach us the way of prudence.

In the first reading the dying Jacob blesses his sons and says of Judah: the sceptre shall not depart from Judah, until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his (Genesis 49:10). From the tribe of Judah would come David, and from David the Messiah.

The Gospel gives us the genealogy of Jesus: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and so on through forty-two generations to Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah (Matthew 1:1–16).

We may be tempted to skip this long list of names. But it is full of meaning. It includes great saints like Abraham and David, and great sinners too. It includes four women, some of them foreigners, and one whose story involved adultery. God's plan passed through all of them.

This tells us that God can write salvation through crooked lines. Our family history may have its own sins, wounds and shames. God is not ashamed to enter it. Jesus took a real human family tree, with all its brokenness, to heal it from within.

Today, let us thank God for our ancestors who handed on the faith, and pray for those in our family line who need healing and mercy. And let us pray with the Church: O Wisdom, come and teach us the way of prudence. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus had grandparents and great-grandparents, just like you. Pray today for your whole family!

q: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.

And Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah. So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Messiah, fourteen generations.
